---
title: "How do I compare average values across categories?"
---

## The question

How do I compare average values across categories?

## What to check and do

1. Identify one numeric measurement and the group labels. 2. Check the number of observations in each group. 3. Calculate grouped means and compare the differences with units.

## Worked example: iris

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
answer <- ru_apply("group_means", data=d,
                   x="Sepal.Length", group="Species")
stopifnot(nrow(answer)==3, all(answer$n==50))
```

The output shows three flower-species averages. It describes those samples; it does not show that species membership caused a particular value.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("group_means", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", group="category_column")
```

If no group column exists, report only an overall mean. A question about difference significance requires a separate inferential method.

## Optional Palmer penguins example

This dataset requires the separately installed `palmerpenguins` package. It is not silently downloaded or substituted.

```r
if (requireNamespace("palmerpenguins", quietly=TRUE)) {
  birds <- ru_data("penguins")
  ru_apply("group_means", birds, x="bill_length_mm", group="species")
}
```

## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("group_means")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
